name: Red-crested Pochard
rangeDescription: Breeds from europe (iberian peninsula northward to southern denmark and poland) eastward to central asia (northwestern china and western mongolia); somewhat local in europe, more widespread to east; resident in southwestern europe; elsewhere, winters from eastern mediterranean eastward to northern india, south-central china, and northern myanmar
description: A diving duck of larger lakes and reservoirs, especially with fringing reeds. Male striking and unmistakable with large, rounded, rusty-orange head, long red bill, and black breast.

name: Tasmanian Boobook
rangeDescription: Tasmania and islands in bass strait
description: Small brownish owl with dark ‘glasses’ surrounding eyes. Fairly common in a wide variety of habitats on Tasmania.

name: Black Harrier
rangeDescription: Arid grassland of southern namibia, southwestern botswana, and south africa
description: A striking, mostly dark harrier with large white panels in the underwings, a white rump, and bands on the tail. The juvenile is brown with white flashes in the underwings and has a heavily-streaked chest.

name: Cryptic Forest-Falcon
rangeDescription: Rainforest of brazil and northeastern bolivia
description: Beautiful forest-falcon, typically very difficult to see. Has a gray head and back, bare red facial skin, and white underparts with gray bars on the breast.

name: Gray-headed Warbler
rangeDescription: Cloud forest of coastal mountains of northeastern venezuela
description: Rare and endangered, a bright yellow warbler with gray head, very short white eyebrow, and orange legs. Sexes similar.

name: Red-bellied Grackle
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia
description: Unmistakable Colombian endemic: large, long-tailed, and all-black with a bright red belly and piercing yellow eye. Sexes similar.

name: Tibetan Eared-Pheasant
rangeDescription: Rhododendron forest of southern tibet and adjacent northeastern india
description: Distinctive slate-gray pheasant with a bright red face, scraggly fan-shaped tail, and bizarre white whiskers (the namesake “ears”). Also note black cap, pale gray rump, and whitish belly.

name: Scalloped Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil to northeastern argentina, northeastern uruguay, and southeastern paraguay
description: Medium-sized woodcreeper with a short, slightly decurved pinkish bill. Found in humid and montane forests, including Araucaria forests, where it typically forages in the canopy.

name: Speckled Rail
rangeDescription: Locally in lowlands of south america east of the andes
description: Very rare and poorly known, but likely widely overlooked, small rail of the southern cone from SE Brazil to central Argentina. Its secretive nature makes it difficult to understand its habitat and habits, but timing of records, combined with records from the middle of downtown Buenos Aires and São Paolo, suggest it is at least somewhat migratory.

name: Olive-green Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of the guianas and adjacent northern brazil (amazonas)
description: Small, uncommon flycatcher of rainforest canopy. Plain, inconspicuous, and unobtrusive; occurs in tall forest, especially on sandy soils, and may also be found in shorter-stature forest on similar soil types.

name: Bougainville White-eye
rangeDescription: Bougainville (northwestern solomon islands)
description: Small social songbird, often encountered foraging in upper levels of forest. Mostly olive-green above with a yellow undertail.

name: Indian Grassbird
rangeDescription: Western nepal to northern india, bangladesh, and northern myanmar
description: Secretive long-tailed babbler. Black-and-white streaking on neck is distinctive if seen well.

name: Kolombangara Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of kolombangara (west-central solomon islands)
description: A small warbler with a dark cap and eye-stripe and a yellow eyebrow. Strongly yellow below, dark chestnut brown above.

name: White-faced Nunbird
rangeDescription: Locally in andean foothills of western colombia to northwestern peru
description: Rare and elusive denizen of Andean cloud forest; found at higher elevations than any other puffbird. Distinctive; note especially the stout, black bill bordered by white feathers, chestnut underparts, and red eye.

name: Papuan Nightjar
rangeDescription: Lowlands of new guinea, including salawati (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea)
description: A widespread nightjar of lowland forest and edge. Distinctive white chevron in the throat.

name: Streak-crowned Antvireo
rangeDescription: Far southeastern honduras, eastern nicaragua, and costa rica
description: This plump little forest bird has a large head and short tail. Not striking, but distinctive in limited range.

name: Himalayan Buzzard
rangeDescription: Breeds from the western himalayas in northern india eastward to montane south-central china (sichuan and gansu); winters to southeast asia
description: A large hawk with a confusing range and unclear identification criteria. Resident in the Himalayas and a breeder in adjacent areas of the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau.

name: Seychelles Swiftlet
rangeDescription: Seychelles (mahé, praslin, and la digue)
description: Small gray swift with a slightly paler rump and belly. Flight is fast but erratic, with the wings pushed forward.

name: Gray Friarbird
rangeDescription: Eastern lesser sundas (kisar, leti, and moa)
description: A large gray-brown honeyeater with a long heavy bill and bluish-gray bare skin below the eye. Brown all over, but paler on the underparts.

name: Great Knot
rangeDescription: Northeastern siberia; winters to india, southeastern asia, philippines, and australia
description: Medium-sized, stocky shorebird found almost exclusively on coastal mudflats during migration, seldom inland. Distinctive adult in breeding plumage has a brick-orange upperwing patch, blackish back, and chest with black mottling.
